name: Peter N. Salib
meta_description: Peter N. Salib works on law and AI risk. W. Ronald Robins Professor of Law, University of Houston; Executive Co-Director, Center for Law & AI Risk; Contributing Editor, Lawfare.
bio: I work on what law and legal institutions can do to reduce existential and other societal-scale risks from advanced AI. A running theme is law as an alignment technology: extending legal rights and duties to powerful AI systems can give them reasons to behave prosocially, and may make catastrophic outcomes less likely than technical training alone.

My scholarship appears in the University of Chicago, Virginia, Michigan, Northwestern, Texas, and Washington University law reviews. AI Rights, written with Simon Goldstein, is forthcoming from Cambridge University Press.

I am the W. Ronald Robins Professor of Law and Associate Professor of Law (with tenure) at the {uh}, and Founder and Executive Co-Director of the {clair}. I am also a Law and Policy Advisor to the {cais}, a Visiting Senior Fellow at the {lawai}, a Senior Visiting Scholar at {forethought}, and a Contributing Editor at {lawfare}. Before teaching I was a Climenko Fellow at Harvard Law School, practiced at Sidley Austin, and clerked for Judge Frank H. Easterbrook. You can reach me at {email}.
